arxiv-2603-20531: Mason and Anand show that language models sound most sure of themselves when they make things up. They test four model families, from OLMo-3 to Mistral. In each, self reported confidence falls as accuracy rises. AUC scores stay below chance in every family. They prove this is a limit of observation, not just skill. A supervisor who sees only output text cannot tell honest text from smooth fakes. No training scheme based on such a supervisor can reach honest behavior. A tensor interface is offered as a way out.
arxiv-2603-20831: Garncarek and co-authors study local verification of graph properties with proofs that may contain errors. In locally checkable proofs, nodes accept or reject based on nearby labels. First they tackle cycle existence in a graph. Three labels and view distance one suffice, and this is tight. A new gadget encodes direction with two labels at distance three. They then build refix, a tool that hardens verifiers against corrupted labels. Lower bounds tie the error count to the view distance needed.
arxiv-2603-20931: Kim and co-authors learn a data driven model of a controlled vibrating composite plate. Exact modeling is hard because the plate is orthotropic and its damping is unknown. They build surrogate models from measured input and output data. Three model types are tried: linear regression, a multilayer perceptron, and a gated recurrent unit. The perceptron gives an acceptable match to the real system. It captures nonlinear effects in the plate's input and output behavior. The study shows machine learning can stand in for a full physical model here.
arxiv-2603-21031: Liu and co-authors study when self-similar measures of product form admit a Fourier orthonormal basis. The measures come from iterated function systems whose digit set is a direct sum of two blocks of consecutive integers. They prove an exact condition on the contraction ratio for such a basis to exist. The condition involves divisibility constraints tied to the block sizes. This extends earlier work for prime and equal block sizes. In the tile case, they show the basis exists exactly when the set is a translation tile.
arxiv-2603-21331: Jaber and Jaber present AutoKernel, an open framework that optimizes GPU kernels with an autonomous agent loop. Writing fast GPU kernels is slow, expert work. Given a PyTorch model, AutoKernel profiles it, ranks bottlenecks by Amdahl's law, and refines Triton or CUDA kernels through hundreds of experiments. A five stage correctness harness checks every candidate before any speedup is recorded. The system covers nine kernel types common in transformers. On an H100, its Triton kernels beat PyTorch eager and torch.compile on most tested setups, by up to several times.
arxiv-2603-21431: López Neumann and Nowak link two things in higher group cohomology: positive functionals and cocycles. They extend a classic construction of Gelfand, Naimark, and Segal to higher degrees. That tool lets them say when higher cohomology of this type vanishes. Vanishing turns into a question of extending positive functionals. They also show that a spectral gap test for the one-sided Laplacian can detect vanishing, under mild conditions.
arxiv-2603-21631: Yu and co-authors use a neural network to design control pulses that fight crosstalk inside superconducting CZ gates. Qubits disturb each other during multi-qubit work, and hardware fixes scale poorly. Their physics-guided framework pairs a hardware-aware pulse form with a Hamiltonian-based goal that tracks crosstalk shifts. The search favors smooth pulses that labs can build. In simulations, it beat a Krotov baseline on fidelity and smoothness under matched limits. Gains were largest for worst-case fidelity when conditions were perturbed, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-21831: González-Calvin and co-authors smooth polygonal chains into curves that still pass exactly through every vertex. Standard mollification rounds a path but loses the vertices, which breaks waypoint fidelity. Their directional mollification builds infinitely smooth curves that stay close to the chain and interpolate its points. Changing one segment affects the output only in a small, known neighborhood. The method also gives closed-form bounds on curvature. A wider family unifies both versions, with uses in robotics, graphics, and CNC machining.
arxiv-2603-21931: Wagner and co-authors regularize neural radiance fields for satellite images, where plain models bend the geometry to fit the photos. Their SatGeo-NeRF adds three fixes that work with many base models. One aligns surface normals inferred from depth with the gravity axis, favoring locally flat ground. A second forces a coarse-to-fine learning order for the geometry. A third supervises depth early in training to steady it. On the DFC2019 reconstruction benchmark, mean altitude error fell by about 14 percent and 12 percent against two strong baselines, they report.
arxiv-2603-22231: Jiang and co-authors present GEM-Rec, a generative recommender that also handles ad revenue. Generative recommenders like TIGER retrieve items from semantic codes. They ignore bids and monetization. GEM-Rec builds both goals into the generated sequence. Control tokens split two choices: whether to show an ad, and which item to show. The model learns placement patterns from past interaction logs. A bid-aware decoding step then injects live bids at inference time. The authors prove higher bids never hurt an ad's chance of being shown.
arxiv-2603-22331: Dayan adds formal safety guarantees to wildfire spread prediction for evacuation planning. Dayan applies conformal risk control, which bounds the false negative rate with finite-sample guarantees. Three model families are compared: tabular, a small U-Net, and a graph hybrid. With plain thresholds, they catch only 7 to 72 percent of true spread. With conformal control, all reach the safety target. The spatial models flag about 15 percent of pixels for the same coverage. The graph model's extra complexity buys no gain over the U-Net.
arxiv-2603-22431: Cassese studies the best constants in Korn's inequality through the lens of the calculus of variations. He adapts tools from the study of the Beurling-Ahlfors transform to the problem. In two dimensions he obtains a bound that is sharp up to a small factor. In general he shows the constant admits a bound that does not grow with dimension. He also proves a weighted version of the inequality that stays dimension-free for a broad class of weights.
arxiv-2603-22831: Pei, Yue, and Zheng build an option pricing model under the G-expectation framework. G-expectation handles model uncertainty as a sublinear expectation. Their unified risk-neutral method yields a nonlinear version of the Black-Scholes equation. A log transform of asset price gives a second form that is cheaper to solve. For that form, they design explicit and implicit finite difference schemes. The schemes are proven consistent, stable, monotone, and convergent. Numeric examples confirm high accuracy and better efficiency.
arxiv-2603-23031: Kothalawala, Koehler, and Farhan speed up maximum common subgraph computation by exploiting symmetry. The problem finds the largest shared part of two graphs. Symmetry can prune search, but past methods used only one graph's symmetries. Their framework breaks symmetries in both the variable and value graphs. Modular symmetries come from local neighborhood structure. Pruning cuts isomorphic subtrees while keeping optimality exact. Benchmark tests beat the prior top method, RRSplit. More cases are solved, with far less time and search.
arxiv-2603-24531: Kalita and co-authors argue that new physical computing devices deserve new models of computation, not just ports of old ones. Exotic devices are often forced to run Boolean circuits or neuromorphic schemes, which may waste what makes them special. The team sets out a methodology for deriving a model of computation and a domain specific language matched to a device's own capabilities. They illustrate the approach with bosonic computing, realised by a physical multi-component interferometer, as their worked case study.
arxiv-2603-24631: Kim and co-authors diagnose why code agents fail even after reaching the right code. Pass rates alone cannot explain the remaining failures on SWE-bench. Their TRAJEVAL tool splits agent trajectories into search, read, and edit stages aligned with the reference patch. Across 16,758 trajectories from three architectures and seven models, the dominant failure is not localisation. Most failures on capable models reach and edit the correct functions yet still produce wrong patches. The largest theme is coherence collapse, where agents overwrite good edits; a checkpoint recovers several lost solutions.
arxiv-2603-25331: Bora and co-authors estimate jet power in two flat-spectrum radio quasars from their full light spectra. Such quasars rank among the most violent objects known. Data from four observatories cover each source in a flaring year. Four particle models are fit: a broken power law, a curved log-parabola, and two with energy-tied timescales. All four give jet powers of the same rough size. That steadiness contrasts with a cousin class where model choice swings power a hundredfold. Low electron break energies explain the calm.
arxiv-2603-25431: Pikovsky asks when a web of phase oscillators acts in a conservative way. Such a web is conservative if its phase volume stays fixed as motion unfolds. He derives a broad test for pairwise couplings, based on a pair-Hamiltonian idea. Two classic families get checked: Winfree-style and Kuramoto-Daido-style coupling. Big conservative webs show a near-mirror Lyapunov spectrum, though not the exact mirror of true Hamiltonian flow. The notion stretches to three-way and four-way couplings as well.
arxiv-2603-25531: Roop and co-authors carve a decidable slice out of Signal Temporal Logic for checking cyber-physical systems. Full static checks of STL are undecidable, so teams fall back on run-time tests. Their SSTL samples signals at fixed ticks and rests on a signal invariance hypothesis. That hypothesis is exactly what makes an STL claim match its SSTL twin. A translation into a predicate form of LTL opens the SPIN checker. A 33-node heart model shows the route works.
arxiv-2603-25631: Basheikh and co-authors survey clinicians on type 1 diabetes care and glucose data. Their two-part questionnaire went to health professionals in diabetes roles in the United Kingdom. Nineteen people completed it. The first part asked how they rank and apply current clinical guidelines. The second asked how well patients read glucose monitor data and act on it. The authors report that blood glucose control ranks first in the guidance. They also find that advice is often tailored to each patient.
arxiv-2603-25731: Straight and co-authors set limits on dark matter scattering off protons using the cosmic microwave background. They use profile likelihoods, a frequentist tool that avoids prior effects. In Bayesian fits, when the cross section or the interacting share nears zero, other parameters go free. This inflates the limits, the authors show. With Planck 2018 data, the Bayesian method consistently overstates the bounds on the cross section. The authors recommend adding frequentist checks to Bayesian limits for models prone to this bias.
arxiv-2603-25931: Meyarian and co-authors present DiReCT, a post-training method that makes generated videos obey physics better. Flow-matching generators often break basic physics while looking smooth. Contrastive training could help, but text prompts tangle scene content with physical behavior. That tangle makes the contrastive signal fight the main objective. DiReCT splits the signal into two scales. One uses far-off negatives for broad separation. The other builds hard negatives that share the scene but change one physical trait. Applied to Wan 2.1, physical commonsense scores rose by 16.7 percent.
arxiv-2603-26131: Ko and co-authors present IBEX, a compression design for CXL memory expanders. Expanders add memory over links like PCIe, but system limits cap how far they scale. IBEX compresses only cold data blocks and leaves hot data plain. Its key trick is cheap tracking of which pages are cold, with little metadata traffic. A shadowed promotion scheme softens the cost when data turns hot again. Packed metadata and grouped blocks save internal bandwidth. Speedups reach 1.28 to 1.40 times over the best prior designs, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-26431: de Montella and Sager build adjoint-friendly stand-ins for the expected information gain in experiment design. The setting is parameter estimation for controlled systems of ordinary differential equations. Fisher criteria fit adjoint methods but stay local and can mislead under strong nonlinearity. The true information gain is sound yet costly and lacks an adjoint form. Their two surrogates split the gain by a chain rule and swap in tractable posterior forms. One matches the true gain exactly in the linear-Gaussian case.
arxiv-2603-26531: Zhu and co-authors present a way to take sharp fluorescence images through scattering material. Scattering blurs optical images at depth, which limits a key diagnostic tool. Their method fires many random light patterns at the sample, then rebuilds the image from local speckle copies. Aligning those copies and computing pixel-wise variance recovers fine detail. It works for wide-field one-photon imaging and for two-photon imaging with a scanned speckle field and one-pixel detector. They report better resolution and convergence than standard autocorrelation methods.
arxiv-2603-26631: Lin, Duan, and Huang study how buyers game the social signals that sellers use for personalised pricing. Sellers can learn a new buyer's tastes from friends' purchases, thanks to homophily in social ties. Buyers who know this may reshape their visible interactions to dodge higher prices. The team models a two-buyer network with two layers of hidden information. They find only high-preference buyers tend to manipulate, and the move can leave those buyers worse off. Sellers, in turn, can gain by pricing with the gaming in mind.
arxiv-2603-26731: Vilas, Schaumlöffel, and Roig ask how much scene context a single object carries inside vision-language models. They show models lone objects on masked backgrounds and test two skills: naming the fine scene type and the broad indoor-outdoor class. Both skills beat chance, and the same object traits that help humans also help the models. Skill at one level does not promise skill at the other, and the coupling varies by model. Objects whose inner form stays steady without a background support the best guesses.
arxiv-2603-27031: Eustachon tests a recent conjecture about the Lee-Yang model through long-range deformations. Non-unitary minimal models were conjectured to arise as fixed points of scalar theories with complex interactions. Eustachon studies two long-range constructions perturbatively, one from the minimal model side. The other starts from its Landau-Ginzburg description. For higher cases beyond Lee-Yang, the two constructions clash with each other. The Lee-Yang case itself behaves like the long-range Ising model instead. The variation thus supports the conjecture only at its base case.
arxiv-2603-27131: Shook and co-authors observe bistable fourth-sound resonance in superfluid helium-3 B inside nanofluidic channels. The channels confine the fluid to widths of 750 to 1800 nm, near the coherence length scale. A strong drive softens the resonance as drive grows. The team reads this as flow suppressing the superfluid gap itself. Their device model converts resonance size into superfluid velocity. One critical velocity matches the point where the along-flow gap part hits zero. A Ginzburg-Landau model agrees with the scaled values.
arxiv-2603-27331: Guan and co-authors build SACRED, a dataset for classifying types of connectedness in online spirituality. Social scientists lacked usable online data for this abstract classification task. The team annotated multimedia, multimodal, multilingual material with social scientist partners. Thirteen popular language models were tested beside rule-based and fine-tuned systems. DeepSeek-V3 led text classification with 79.19 percent accuracy on the Quora set. GPT-4o-mini led the vision side with a 63.99 percent F1 score. The study also surfaced a previously unnoticed connectedness type.
arxiv-2603-27431: Llerena-Córdova studies special maps from genus-two surfaces to a line. A fixed divisor embeds the surface in projective space. Some flat subspaces project the surface in a Galois way. Those subspaces are known to split into projective pieces. The author computes the size of each piece. The case treated here comes from symmetry groups of the surface. The result pins down the shape of the Galois set. It adds detail to a known structure theorem.
arxiv-2603-27531: Zhang and co-authors present OmniColor for coloring line art under mixed controls. Users may give hints by place, by reference image, or both. OmniColor sorts signals into two kinds. Aligned inputs use dual-path encoding with a boundary loss. Reference inputs use a vision-language encoder with redundancy cuts. A gating module weighs the two streams when they clash. Tests show strong control, quality, and time stability. The tool targets pro content workflows.
arxiv-2603-27631: Tinati and Tu build limit theory for pretraining from unlabeled data. Models learn features first, then fine-tune for a task. Learned features are fixed only up to a symmetry. That twist breaks plain two-stage math. Tools from curved geometry handle the core quantities instead. A link through orbit sameness ties them to test risk. The team pins down the limit law for that risk. Case studies cover spectral methods, factor models, and mixtures.
arxiv-2603-27831: Ji and co-authors quantify how GPU data centers can flex power use. AI growth strains grids as demand climbs fast. A rolling-horizon scheduler weighs IT load and cooling together. Cooling shifts cut demand briefly at about thirty dollars per megawatt-hour. Backfill job moves cut demand at similar low prices. Reordering or delaying jobs costs far more. Perfect foresight of the job queue boosts flexibility greatly.
arxiv-2603-28131: Chaimongkon and six co-authors model how the scalar meson f0(980) forms in proton-proton collisions at 5.02 TeV. Their UrQMD transport model first reproduces kaon output, then a coalescence step merges kaon-antikaon pairs into f0(980) and a0(980). A momentum window near 0.365 GeV/c best matches the ALICE spectrum and yield. The fit supports reading f0(980) as a late-stage kaon molecule formed near freeze-out. The setup also covers small collision systems.
arxiv-2603-28231: Dharmaputra, Curumi, and Noiray test perforated acoustic black holes as dampers for thermoacoustic instability in a hydrogen combustor. Such instabilities shake gas turbines and spoil flame measurements. Standard dampers work only in narrow frequency bands. The team printed several black hole designs, measured them, and matched a simple transfer-matrix model to the data. An optimized damper fitted to the test rig cut pressure oscillation levels sharply across all run conditions.
arxiv-2603-28331: Yu and three co-authors introduce a workshop method that pits design against policy to spark better teamwork on new technology. Design-Policy Adversarial Futuring stages structured clashes between the two viewpoints around future scenarios. A trial workshop with 12 researchers used self-driving mobility as the test case. The format surfaced harms that shift over time and turned abstract rules into concrete cases. It also gave wild ideas a fair hearing while keeping policy talk grounded.
arxiv-2603-28531: Hornick and Pelinovsky chart families of solitary waves in a system coupling a KdV long wave to a linear Schrödinger short wave. Starting from lone KdV solitons, they follow a chain of pitchfork bifurcations. The first branch pairs the soliton with the short wave's ground state and provably minimizes energy at fixed mass and momentum. Later branches use excited states instead. The first two branches match exact solutions long used in the literature.
arxiv-2603-28831: Joshi and co-authors sort types of mixed swarms of uncrewed vehicles and test how mix affects strength. They group swarms by three traits. These are agent nature, hardware build, and the space where they work. A review of past work shows that a smart mix boosts swarm results. Mixed swarms can swap roles, use many sensor types, and adapt fast. The authors also note hard parts, like links, energy use, and control fit. They give design notes for swarms that are ready for real tasks.
arxiv-2603-29331: Xu and co-authors map how dwarf galaxies connect to dark matter halos. Their method, PAC, mixes deep photometric and spectroscopic data. It measures excess photometric objects around spectroscopic tracers. They model 349 measurements from DESI and DECaLS data. The stellar-to-halo mass relation reaches halos near a hundred million solar masses. It shows an upturn near ten billion solar masses. That upturn means rising star-formation efficiency in small halos. Central red galaxies dominate the low-mass regime.
arxiv-2603-30031: Di Gioia frames agent deliberation as a cost problem in his Triadic Cognitive Architecture. Tool-using agents must choose which source to query and when to stop and act. Unchecked agents over-query under congestion and stall under time decay. His model prices information by signal quality and live network load. A stopping boundary follows from an HJB-style rule. In two test worlds, the method gains 36 and 33 points over greedy baselines. Time-to-action drops while accuracy holds.
arxiv-2604-00031: Saidd builds a modular reinforcement-learning system for currency trading that models real trading frictions, including spreads, commissions, slippage, rollover costs, and margin-triggered liquidation. Its reward splits into 11 logged parts, and its 10-action interface masks out trades that break margin rules. Tested on euro-dollar data, the full reward setup reaches a Sharpe ratio of 0.765 with a 57 percent return, while wider action choices lift returns but lower the Sharpe through extra trading.
arxiv-2604-00431: Dong and colleagues push twin-field quantum key distribution to 1 megabit per second over 200 kilometres. Twin-field schemes boost secure key rates across city distances through square-root scaling, and multiplexing parallel channels could raise rates further. Each channel normally needs its own ultra-stable laser and phase-locked loops, which scale poorly. The team instead uses two independent integrated dissipative Kerr soliton microcombs, one at each end, as multi-wavelength sources, with high-visibility single-photon interference across all channels.
arxiv-2604-00731: Hatem and colleagues built STCALIR, a framework that turns raw Algerian legal documents into test collections for judging search and ranking systems. It follows the Cranfield pattern of topics, documents, and relevance judgments, but automates retrieval and filtering to cut hand annotation by 99 percent. Tested against the Mr. TyDi benchmark, its machine-made judgments ranked systems in close agreement with human judgments.
arxiv-2604-00931: Yang and team propose PsychAgent, an agent that keeps learning from past work for a self-growing therapy guide. A memory-aided planning engine supports long multi-session work with therapy flow. A skill growth engine extracts new hands-on skills from past therapy records, and a boosted uptake step folds those skills into the model via rejection fine-tuning. Side-by-side tests show it beats strong general language models and field standards on every stated area.
arxiv-2604-01331: Bai and Fang pin down which global nilpotent cones fail to be reduced, meaning their equations carry extra nilpotent fuzz, not a clean object. Under coprimality conditions, the cone for an L-twisted GLr Hitchin fibration over a curve of genus at least 2 is nowhere reduced. That holds whether L is the canonical bundle or has degree above twice the genus minus 2. The same verdict holds for one-dimensional sheaves on K3, abelian and del Pezzo surfaces. They also characterize when a Beauville-Mukai fiber has primitive homology class.
arxiv-2604-02731: Thingna, Xu and Manzano formulate a polaron-transformed version of the canonically consistent quantum master equation for open quantum systems under strong system-bath coupling. The base equation moves beyond weak coupling while keeping the numerical cost of standard master equations. The polaron transform pushes accessible coupling strengths from moderate to ultra-strong. Applied to the spin-boson model, the method agrees excellently with exact TEMPO simulations.
arxiv-2604-02831: Mao and four colleagues report an unusual tidal dwarf galaxy candidate, Holmberg IX, studied across many wavelengths. Deep hydrogen-alpha maps plus archival data on dust, gas, and stars reveal a dust shortage at odds with rich gas and metals. The stars are globally young, with strong far-ultraviolet but weak hydrogen-alpha light. Assuming a normal initial mass function, the galaxy was born about 130 million years ago in a burst that then stopped. Current star formation occurs only at the outskirts.
arxiv-2604-03231: Deria and colleagues fuse two kinds of vision encoders, contrastive and self-supervised, to strengthen vision-language models. Their CoME-VL framework merges the encoders at the representation level, cutting redundancy and aligning token grids before feeding compact visual tokens to a language model. Tests show about 5 percent gains on both visual understanding and grounding tasks, with leading detection results on RefCOCO.
arxiv-2604-03631: Peng and Feng compare single-agent and multi-agent vision language models for auto coding of screen clips in group learning, using the ICAP framework. They test leading closed-source models and an open-source model in single- and multi-agent settings. These include a three-agent workflow system and a self-deciding system inspired by ReAct. Both multi-agent frameworks beat single models on scene and action spotting, with the workflow agent best on scenes and the self-deciding agent best on actions.
arxiv-2604-03831: Ravindran Kannan and colleagues proved that singular value decomposition can denoise nearest-neighbor search when data sit in a low-dimensional subspace plus Gaussian noise. When noise stays below a threshold tied to subspace dimension, SVD recovers the true nearest neighbor. Above that threshold, the true neighbor may not even be identifiable from noisy data, a matching lower bound. A third result shows naive search on noisy data fails in regimes where SVD still succeeds.
arxiv-2604-04031: Yuan Guo and team built an environment-aware near-field channel estimation plan for joined sensing and comms systems with huge antenna arrays. A new channel knowledge map, the virtual object map, stores virtual scene objects to capture main multi-path parts from static objects. A sensing-aided training routine pairs downlink pilots with single-site echoes for dynamic targets, plus coded user feedback. Joint work on static and dynamic parts beat older schemes on scores and data rates.
arxiv-2604-04131: Paulo Akira F. Enabe introduced Profile-Then-Reason, a bounded execution framework for language-model agents that use external tools. Instead of recomputing reasoning after every observation, the model first drafts an explicit workflow, guarded operators run it, a verifier checks the trace, and repair runs only when the workflow fails. In the nominal case the pipeline needs just two language-model calls, three at worst. Against ReAct across six benchmarks and four models, it won the pairwise exact-match comparison in 16 of 24 configurations.
arxiv-2604-04331: Shen and colleagues rebuild static 3D scenes from moving-object video. Current methods lean on background alone and fail where moving objects hide parts. Their GA-GS method segments and removes moving regions, then uses a diffusion model to paint in hidden areas as pseudo-ground-truth supervision. A learnable authenticity score tunes opacity during rendering, balancing real and generated regions. The team built Trajectory-Match, recorded by a fixed-path robot with and without moving objects. GA-GS leads rivals on both, above all under large occlusions.
arxiv-2604-04731: Pai, Namboothiri and Mathew analyze two horizon thermodynamics versions. In modified gravity, the Clausius rule gains an extra entropy-production term. Two versions exist: Eling, Guedens and Jacobson's Rindler horizon approach, and the cosmological apparent horizon version in FLRW spacetime. Though both employ the same entropy balance relations, the origin and role of each term differs. In the Rindler setup, the extra term follows from Bianchi rule, whereas the apparent-horizon approach introduces it to recover Friedmann equations. The latter part enters motion equations, while the former does not.
arxiv-2604-04931: Nordström and eight colleagues revisit local feature matching, a core step in 3D vision systems such as Structure-from-Motion, where progress lagged behind newer reconstruction models. Those newer models scaled with huge datasets, while matching models trained only on a few mid-sized sets. Their LoMa approach combines large diverse data mixtures, modern training recipes, larger models, and more compute for remarkable gains. The work argues matching deserves the same data-driven scaling that lifted feed-forward reconstruction.
arxiv-2604-05231: Brady and four colleagues find a new definition of colored edge graphs of finite algebras in the case of minimal Taylor algebras. Their definition includes the graphs that Bulatov invented for this area. They reprove the main results of Bulatov's theory in the case of minimal Taylor algebras in their own setting. Compared with the more general case of smooth algebras that Bulatov considered, their setting yields several simplifications.
arxiv-2604-05931: Sun and seven colleagues fix two flaws in successor representations for visual unsupervised reinforcement learning, where agents must handle new tasks with no extra training. Saliency-guided dynamics tasks first learn what matters in the scene, then a fast consistency policy steers skill-based actions. On 16 tasks across 4 ExORL data sets, their SRCP tops zero-shot rivals and fits varied base methods.
arxiv-2604-06031: Notaro's 2026 paper isolates maximal n-ladders to attack Ditor's 1984 question. An n-ladder is a lattice with at most n lower covers. Ditor proved a size bound for n-ladders and asked whether it can always be reached. The forcing axiom Add makes every maximal n-ladder reach the bound, answering Ditor positively for every n. He shows no maximal 3-ladder of the size need exist, yet one follows under a dominating-number assumption. Clubsuit yields a maximal 3-ladder of breadth 2, and diamond one destructible by Suslin tree forcing.
arxiv-2604-06231: Zhou and six colleagues build DBCooker, a language-model system that writes database-native functions, where generic generators hallucinate or miss context. A characterization module gathers declarations, picks units needing special coding, and traces dependencies between units. Synthesis uses a pseudo-code plan generator, a hybrid blank-filling model with probabilistic priors, and three-level validation for syntax, standards, and meaning. Adaptive orchestration sequences these steps using histories of similar functions. DBCooker beats rivals on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB by 34.55 percent, and synthesizes functions missing from the latest SQLite.
arxiv-2604-06431: Arcis, González, and Márquez study quasisymmetric functions in superspace, building on earlier ones with commuting and anticommuting symbols. The algebra is the fixed points of the symmetric group's quasisymmetrizing action. They complete the classical Hopf ladder in superspace with their noncommuting-variable version. That algebra is a Hopf superalgebra, with a Q-basis and a monomial basis indexed by set supercompositions. Minimal poset points yield the superpermutation Hopf superalgebra, version of Malvenuto-Reutenauer. Products and coproducts use super-shuffles and global descents; abelianization derives the fundamental product formula.
arxiv-2604-07131: Chow and Kasahara dissect overidentified instrumental-variable estimation, where the weighting matrix quietly picks which average effect is estimated. They show the estimate is a weighted mix of instrument-specific Wald estimates, with exact weights and a test for when those weights stay nonnegative. Efficient weighting, they add, imposes a penalty for heterogeneity. Their representativeness-targeting estimator instead aims directly at a researcher-chosen mix, and it performs well on Tennessee STAR and patent-leniency examples.
arxiv-2604-07331: Mao and four colleagues introduce RoSHI, a wearable suit for capturing human motion in the wild to train robots. It fuses cheap sparse motion sensors with Project Aria glasses, combining occlusion-proof body tracking with egocentric mapping that anchors long motions in a global frame. The system estimates full 3D pose and body shape from the wearer's own viewpoint. On agile activities it beats other egocentric baselines, matches a leading external-camera baseline, and yields motion data usable for real humanoid policies.
arxiv-2604-07631: Neely and five colleagues describe a programmable, dynamic two-dimensional quasiperiodic optical lattice for quantum simulation with ultracold atoms. Programmable control of lattice beam phases via Floquet engineering opens a wide space of systems, with full translational and phasonic control beyond the lattice recoil velocity. Their scheme heavily suppresses phase noise: over 70 dB across the DC to 60 Hz band, with suppression up to 5 kHz. Phase modulation bandwidth reaches 350 kHz. The setup paves a path toward direct observation plus control of quantum dynamics in quasicrystals, including changes to rotational symmetry.
arxiv-2604-07831: Yang and nine colleagues red-team screen-based AI agents with a practical black-box attack. Older attacks need white-box access that commercial systems do not offer, while prompt injection increasingly fails against stronger safety alignment. Their semantic-level UI element injection overlays harmless, safety-aligned screen elements onto screenshots to mislead the agent's visual grounding. A modular editor-overlapper-victim pipeline plus iterative search picks the best cumulative overlay. Tests across 19 victim models in eight families show tuned overlays beat random ones by a wide margin.
arxiv-2604-08131: Kuntur and six colleagues benchmark graph neural networks against non-graph machine learning methods for misinformation detection under controlled conditions. Rapid online falsehood spread drove ever more complex tools, including large language models and hybrid architectures, whose compute cost and rollout limits raise real concerns. Lightweight graph architectures, GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, and ChebNet, are tested against logit models, support vector machines, and MLPs across seven datasets in English, Indonesian, and Polish. Every model uses the same TF-IDF features to isolate network impact, with F1 score and run time reported.
arxiv-2604-08931: Özdemir and Oztop test whether a tutor student team creates synergy for language model problem solving, inspired by social mind growth. Two agents from the same model take uneven roles: a student builds and refines coding answers while a tutor gives ordered feedback without answer keys. Their PETITE setup draws better work from one model through matching roles rather than stronger bosses or mixed teams. On the APPS coding benchmark it matches or beats Self-Consistency, Self-Refine, Multi-Agent Debate, and Multi-Agent Review while using far fewer tokens.
arxiv-2604-09031: Donkiewicz studies how to pick subproblems as needed in Benders decomposition for tough network design. Benders splits first-stage master choices from second-stage recourse actions, tuning the master problem with cuts over rounds. Solving every task each round is the norm, but with many cases, solving only a chosen subset can save compute. The paper gauges the gain from solving only cut-yielding tasks. Its best scoring and picking method lifts runtime and primal-dual integrals a lot, while random picks perform far worse than full listing.
arxiv-2604-09331: Richardson, Zhang, King, and Drgoňa propose a stable Gaussian process variational autoencoder for training a linear time invariant system from video data. Its mean and covariance derive from that system's definition. That lets it capture the latent process through a chance-based and clear physical model. System parameters are restricted to semi-contracting systems via a free setup, so training can use free optimization. That avoids issues from a non-Hurwitz state matrix. A case study on videos of swirling particles highlights accurate latent state forecasts.
arxiv-2604-09431: Choi, Park, Halilaj, and Kang present muscle motion copying for custom exoskeleton control in impaired gait. General lower-limb exo rules remain constrained by endless data harvest or repeat tuning, curbing patient access. Their device-free framework combines lifelike muscle simulation with reward learning, giving large-scale custom help. Rules make likely walking moves and capture in-patient observed make-up tactics under targeted muscle gaps. Without task-specific tuning, rules produce hip and ankle torque profiles matching human-validated profiles while cutting energy cost across walking speeds.
arxiv-2604-09531: Zhou and five colleagues ask whether synthetic images can teach vision-language models low-level seeing skills that natural datasets under-supply. Their VisionFoundry pipeline takes only a task name, then uses language models to draft questions, answers, and image prompts, renders the images, and filters the results by multimodal checks. Fine-tuning on the resulting 10-task dataset lifts perception scores across three open backbones, gaining about 7 percent on MMVP-pair and about 11 percent on CV-Bench-3D for Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, without harming broader abilities.
arxiv-2604-09731: Wang and Zhou address a speed paradox in tree-based speculative decoding. Drafting and checking big trees can balloon in cost, giving slowdowns as batches grow. Current methods chase token odds while missing that cost. Their SMART method tunes tree growth for end-to-end speedup, growing a node only when its extra gain beats the tree speedup. Training-free and plug-and-play for MSD and EAGLE, SMART adds about 20 percent speedup for multimodal models and about 15 percent for language models. It holds across batching regimes and GPU chips.
arxiv-2604-10031: Li, Shi, and Deng present CoSToM, a causal-aimed steering setup matching language models' Theory of Mind acts with their internal knowledge. Standard benchmarks show promise, but models often fail complex set cases, leaning on prompt props to mimic thought. Causal tracing maps where Theory of Mind marks live inside the model, showing how internal layers encode basic social sense. Aimed firing steering within those key layers then lifts human-like social thought and downstream chat quality, moving from gear reading to active action.
arxiv-2604-10131: Xue and 34 colleagues watch SGR J1935+2154, the only magnetar seen to emit fast radio bursts, during its October 2022 outburst. Insight-HXMT observed it October 13 to November 1, 2022, for 940 kiloseconds, while KM40m watched for 1400 hours from October 15. Overlap yielded 60 magnetar X-ray bursts but only 1 radio burst. One X-ray burst on October 21, MXB 221021, lines up with that radio burst. Its shape differs sharply from earlier joint events from this source. Its properties also differ from bursts with no radio partner, shedding light on magnetar burst physics.
arxiv-2604-10331: Cohen, Nissan, Nissan, and Lellouch present a scalable method for locating buried fiber cables with distributed acoustic sensing and traffic seismic signals. From one end of the fiber, the method fuses sound readings with vehicle paths from video tracking or GPS. Fiber shape comes from cutting mismatch between seen and model strain maps. A matched start plus neural path tuning settles well under real noise and path doubt. Lab and field tests reach sub-meter marks, often tens of cm, agreeing with manual tap checks.
arxiv-2604-10431: Granier, Bacchini, Groselj, and Sironi run two and three dimensional runs of driven magnetic reconnection. Two Lundquist flux tubes merge in a strongly magnetized pair plasma, shedding field energy and speeding particles. Three dimensional runs delay onset versus flat runs, more so under a strong guide field. All runs reach a fast merge stage with a rate just under one tenth and a shared particle cutoff near 50. The particle spectra look alike across runs, with power law slopes in a narrow band.
arxiv-2604-10631: Biazotto and three colleagues mine GitHub to learn how debt tools actually appear in CI/CD pipelines. Automated checks there could make debt work routine. From about 600,000 Travis files and 50,000 scripts they identify 3,684 pipelines using at least one debt tool. Most tools run through an outside script. The most common setup flaw is Absent Feedback, where a tool runs without sending its findings back into the workflow.
arxiv-2604-11031: El Gantouh and three colleagues study input-to-state stability of boundary control systems with endless edge couplings. Using semigroup theory and linear maps on Banach frames, they derive a spectral small-gain test giving exponential decay. They further study Boltzmann-type models on an endless network of crossing circles, with delays, scatter, and junction noise. For this class, a spectral small-gain test on the transmission matrix guarantees fast decay against network noise. They also derive plain bounds for cases and show real use through time-delayed settings.
arxiv-2604-11731: Chakrabarti, Ni, Jiang, and Mallick tackle clustering for nested data, where observations sit inside groups that also carry their own variables. Their Nested Atoms Model, a Bayesian nonparametric method, clusters cells and people jointly, using gene expression at cell level and genotypes at person level. A fast variational inference routine scales it to large data, and on the OneK1K set of 982 people and 1.27 million cells it finds genetically similar groups with matching cell-type profiles.
arxiv-2604-12231: Feng and four colleagues propose Thought-Retriever, a method letting language-model agents draw on arbitrarily long external data without being bound by context length or retrieved chunk counts. Instead of raw chunks, it filters past intermediate responses, stores them as thought memory, and retrieves relevant thoughts for new queries, so memory improves with use. On AcademicEval and two public datasets it beats strong baselines by at least 7.6 percent in F1 and 16 percent in win rate.
arxiv-2604-12331: Moreno and nine colleagues present HyperLiDAR, a lightweight LiDAR segmentation framework based on hyperdimensional computing for on-device adaptation after deployment. Shifting real-world scenes degrade conventional large-network models, which edge devices cannot retrain under tight compute and energy limits. HyperLiDAR learns fast and cheaply, and a buffer selection strategy focuses learning on the most informative points per scan. It matches or beats leading methods while retraining up to 13.8 times faster.
arxiv-2604-12831: Shengding Liu and Qiben Yan build VULCAN, a multi-agent navigation system for indoor fire rescue. Existing vision-based systems suit calm indoor settings and fail badly as fire spreads. VULCAN pairs multi-modal perception with vision-language models for hazard-aware planning. The team extends Habitat-Matterport3D with realistic smoke, heat, and sensor damage. Baselines are tested in normal and fire-driven settings. Results expose failure modes of current methods under fire and stress robust perception for reliable rescue.
arxiv-2604-13031: Montalvo, Goulding, and Greene assemble 6,600 reddened and blue Type-1 quasars from deep optical and infrared imaging to probe what dims the reddened ones. Modeling their light shows reddened quasars suffer far more dust extinction, yet also narrower torus opening angles. Their line strengths point to dust acting near the nucleus rather than across the host galaxy. The pattern suggests dusty gas carried outward along the poles.
arxiv-2604-13131: Saleh and Azghadi build a physics-informed neural network that maps coral reef temperatures below the surface, where satellite readings alone mislead. Fusing satellite sea surface temperature with sparse underwater loggers inside a vertical heat equation, the model learns thermal diffusivity and light attenuation, hitting 0.25 to 1.38 degrees Celsius error at unseen depths. Depth-resolved heat stress falls with depth at Davies Reef, and the model's smooth predictions make its heat-stress values conservative lower bounds.
arxiv-2604-13231: Alfs and nine colleagues propose the first test of sideways antiproton polarization in proton-nucleus collisions, an effect whose existence is unknown today. Polarization would be read through left-right asymmetry in elastic antiproton-proton bounces in the Coulomb Nuclear Interference region. Detailed Monte Carlo models of a CERN setup estimate the sensitivity needed to detect a given degree of polarization, testing the spin structure of the antinucleon-nucleon interaction.
arxiv-2604-13331: Kerdabadi and four colleagues build MedCo, a tool for learning better codes for medical ideas from health records. Code lists often miss links between diagnoses, medicines, and procedures, and rich meaning in text is hard to join with graph form. MedCo mines solid links from records, uses language-model prompts to infer meaning links, and adds written notes for codes and links. Joint training with a text encoder and graph network lifts prediction scores on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.
arxiv-2604-13431: Guo and three colleagues construct, explicitly rather than by existence argument, several objects used in pseudorandomness. These are lossless rank extractors. They also build weak subspace designs and strong blocking sets over finite fields. Their focus is the small-field case. There, field size depends only on rank or codimension, not on ambient dimension. They give the first explicit lossless extractors and weak designs for small rank, with near-best parameters, and blocking sets matching the best non-explicit bounds.
arxiv-2604-13631: Adshead, Maxted, and Hahlin measure fundamental properties of the eclipsing binary CD-27 2812, pairing a Sun-like star with a much fainter M dwarf. Combining TESS light curves with HARPS and NIRPS spectra, plus Gaia parallax and published photometry, they derive model-independent masses and radii for both stars. Near-infrared flux ratios then give effective temperatures near 6,197 kelvin for the primary and 3,770 kelvin for the companion, a rare benchmark for low-mass stellar models.
arxiv-2604-13731: Zheng and eleven colleagues present Doc-V*, an OCR-free agentic tool for questions over multi-page documents. Long, dense documents strain end-to-end models. Passive retrieval pipelines break easily. Doc-V* starts from a thumbnail overview. It then navigates by semantic retrieval and page fetching. Evidence gathers in a working memory that grounds its reasoning. Trained by imitation from expert paths and refined with group relative policy optimization, it beats open-source baselines on five benchmarks. Out-of-domain performance rises by nearly 48 percent over a retrieval baseline.
arxiv-2604-13831: Bar-Gera, Boyles, and Ravner study departure-time choice with varied schedule-delay parameters. Vickrey's classic single-bottleneck equilibrium is unstable under many plausible daily learning dynamics, yet real traffic shows no such instability. The authors ask whether dynamics or a simple assumption explains the gap. Their variant uses a spread of schedule-delay parameters with a monotonic earliness-lateness link. Equilibrium exists and is unique here. Surprisingly, they prove that a broad family of day-to-day dynamics respecting local pressure and order keeping stays unstable here.
arxiv-2604-13931: Hondamuni and colleagues image skyrmions in magnetic thin films coated with chiral molecules. They use wide-field nitrogen-vacancy sensing at room temperature. Pixel-resolved resonance maps plus controlled fields let them nucleate and probe skyrmion states in CoFeB samples again and again. They find changes that depend on handedness and field polarity in skyrmion size, spacing, and shape. That hints at molecular control of spin textures.
arxiv-2604-14031: Collinson studies categories tied to transition systems with algebra and topology. He shows two such categories connect through a contravariant adjunction. It is the most detailed result in a set that varies with shape limits on objects and maps. The work shows how the categories relate under different limits, giving a careful bridge between the algebra and shape sides of transition systems.
arxiv-2604-14331: Eremeev, Said, and Borovitskiy build geometric kernels for matchings, pairings whose discrete, non-Euclidean shape defeats ordinary kernel tools. They first chart all stationary kernels that respect the space's symmetries, then narrow to heat and Matérn families that add a smoothness bias. Naive evaluation would cost super-exponential time, so the team devises a sub-exponential algorithm based on zonal polynomials. A matching-tree link from biology is probed too, yielding negative transfer results and one clear open problem.
arxiv-2604-14431: Dandu presents AndroScanner, an automated pipeline that hunts backend flaws in Android apps by joining static and dynamic analysis. It pulls backend API calls from app packages with apktool, Androguard, and Frida-based instrumentation, then checks them with APIFuzzer for OWASP API Security Top 10 flaws. Across a deliberately vulnerable bank app and a production recruitment app with over 50,000 downloads, the tool pulled 24 APIs and found 5 flaws. One was an unreported zero-day excessive-data-exposure flaw in the production app, disclosed to its team before publication.
arxiv-2604-14631: Jang, Han, and Yoo propose StoryCoder, a system that recasts code-writing questions as coherent natural-language narratives instead of leaving problem details scattered. Each narrative holds a task summary, constraints, and example test cases, shaped by the chosen algorithm and genre. Across 11 models on those three benchmarks, they lift zero-shot pass-at-10 by 18.7 percent on average, a steady gain. Beyond accuracy, narratives steer models toward correct algorithmic strategies, cut implementation errors, and yield more modular code, with gains hinging on narrative coherence and genre alignment.
arxiv-2604-14731: Fransson examines how lattice vibrations, or phonons, can carry magnetic interactions between localized moments in insulators. In metals, roving electrons do this job, but insulators lack such carriers, leaving magnetic order in oxides a puzzle. The paper shows symmetric anisotropic spin-spin coupling arises from every phonon type, while antisymmetric coupling needs broken inversion symmetry. That second channel may explain weak ferromagnetism in chiral copper and cobalt oxides. The coupling barely shifts with temperature when cold, grows linearly when hot, and fades with distance in an oscillating power law.
arxiv-2604-15031: Han and colleagues bring a hypergraph container method to the satisfiability problem, asking whether a logical formula can ever be true. They show that when clauses spread evenly, containers shrink the search space harder and the method runs faster. A weighted view scores each clause by its size, giving a new spread measure for formulas. The paper ties clause spread directly to container speed, turning an even spread into faster solving.
arxiv-2604-15231: Roschewitz and others present RadAgent, an AI agent that uses tools to write chest CT reports step by step. Older vision-language methods hand doctors only a final output, with no step-by-step trace to inspect, validate, or refine. RadAgent's reports carry a fully open trace of middle decisions and tool uses. It beats its 3D vision-language rival CT-Chat, lifting accuracy 5.8 points on macro-F1 and adding a faithfulness score its rival lacks entirely.
arxiv-2604-15731: Piduguralla, Sarkar, Ramachandran, and Peri offer BlockRaFT, a crash-proof frame for blockchain nodes that lifts scale and trust. A RAFT vote picks a lead node, which hands work to followers. No-state jobs sit with the lead, while state jobs get copied and lined up across the group for steady agreement. A side-by-side Merkle tree tweak splits deal runs from tree writes, cutting a big drag. Tests weigh the shared node build against lone-node runs on scale, uptime, and speed.
arxiv-2604-15931: Boris Latosh tests whether Starobinsky inflation survives a minimal scalar extension motivated by scalar-tensor gravity. Solving the background system numerically, he finds the exact Starobinsky branch acts as a finite-time attractor when the extra scalar is at least as heavy as the scalaron. Tensor and scalar modes show a healthy kinetic sector with no gradient instabilities, and speeds match light over the tested range. Curvature spectra stay extraordinarily close to Starobinsky across the scan, with omitted corrections far below the one-in-a-thousand accuracy that matters.
arxiv-2604-16431: Wang introduces an avalanche probe for grokking, the sudden jump from memorizing to generalizing long after training accuracy levels off. His TDU-OFC method turns gradient snapshots into cascade statistics and tracks an effective cascade dimension over time. Across transformers on modular addition and simpler networks on XOR, that dimension crossed the Gaussian baseline of 1 exactly at the generalization jump. It fell through the baseline for one task and rose through it for the other. Runs that never grokked stayed above the baseline, supporting a shared critical picture.
arxiv-2604-16531: Braga, Jimenez and Matarrese ask if a symmetry can order old degeneracy and small-change calm in DHOST theories. An AI-aided search finds one in an image of Einstein gravity. It is a field-based diffeomorphism plus an upward shift of a scalar. Spread over first-order maps, the build pulls that shift back to a local gauge freedom. Under the rules, the spectator, its ghost and their antifields close into a quartet. That quartet adds no counterterm, gauge deformation or anomaly class, and leaves no ghosts.
arxiv-2604-16631: Paganini opens correlation geometry, the framework behind causal fermion systems. The paper aims for a compact, short and clear account of its basic ideas. A key focus is how the framework handles gauge changes, like diffeomorphisms, through unitary match. In spirit, framing a physical system by its link geometry resembles thermodynamics more than quantum theory. Readers need little background to follow it.
arxiv-2604-16731: Napier and colleagues open heliostack, a search tool using nonlinear shift-and-stack for solar system objects. Faint solar system objects light planet origins and growth, yet conventional surveys struggle to detect them. It merges images over longer time spans than ever before, lifting archival and future surveys' find power. Applied to archival Hubble images spanning 15 days in 2003, it fully searches for Cold classic Kuiper Belt Objects. It finds both known sub-threshold objects and adds two new discoveries, the first found in stacks spanning over a day.
arxiv-2604-16831: Chu and colleagues propose cooling many degenerate mechanical modes at once in optomechanical systems beyond the settled sideband regime. The dark-mode effect blocks such cooling, but Duffing moving nonlinearities can overcome it. A second-order curved medium, an optical curve, does ground-state cooling beyond the resolved sideband regime. The dark mode breaks when moving curves of other modes are not very close.
arxiv-2604-17031: Beckmann and Butlin ask which entities linked to a large language model, if any, deserve to be called minds. Working through mechanistic interpretability and recent work on persona vectors, they weigh three candidates. They defend the virtual instance view, arguing attention streams sustain quasi-psychological links across token time, and present two new persona-based views as promising rivals.
arxiv-2604-17131: Qin and eight colleagues build a classifier for three plasma regions around Mars, solar wind, magnetosheath, and induced magnetosphere, using only ion energy spectra from the MAVEN Solar Wind Ion Analyzer. Two networks are tested: a multilayer perceptron and a convolutional network using short temporal sequences. That network cleanly separates all three regions, while the simpler one struggles to separate solar wind from the sheath.
arxiv-2604-17331: Chudy and Woźny present faster ways to evaluate Gauss-Legendre curves, giving new forms for the polynomials and their derivatives in shifted and Jacobi-related bases. Their recurrences yield methods whose cost grows quadratically in degree for a single curve, plus a multipoint scheme scaling with the number of points. The work speeds a classical numerical task that underpins approximation and geometric computation.
arxiv-2604-17431: Besanson models vertical foreclosure in AI inference markets, where advantage lies in inference, distribution, and routing. Two routes need no predatory pricing: quality-of-service bias against downstream rivals and routing bias in assistant tools. A third route, tier-based access bias, follows Anthropic's April 2026 release pattern. Under logit demand with even rivals, the gap grows with quality importance and margins and shrinks with price and entry response. A four-provider mapping points to Google and OpenAI as most exposed, and the paper offers a Neutral Inference conduct framework.
arxiv-2604-17631: de la Fuente and four colleagues study scalable conjugate beamforming methods for group sending in cell-free massive MIMO systems. With fully spread-out precoding, they analyze basic, normalized, and boosted forms within a subgroup-based plan, grouping users by fading likeness for shared channel checks, pilot reuse, and simple coding. Tests show strong layout effects: unicast wins in uniform setups, while subgroup sending becomes vital when users cluster or mix. Normalized beamforming offers a robust tradeoff in most cases.
arxiv-2604-17931: Qu and seven colleagues make agentic reinforcement learning for deep research scalable with LiteResearcher. Hand-crafted synthetic data fails to teach genuine search, while live search during training brings instability and high cost. Their lite virtual world mirrors real search dynamics, supporting a training recipe that keeps improving. The resulting 4-billion-parameter agent beats large open and commercial models, scoring 71.3 percent on GAIA and 78.0 percent on Xbench, both open-source bests.
arxiv-2604-18131: Zhang and seven colleagues train language-model agents to explore unfamiliar digital environments on their own. No human rewards or rules guide the agent at run time. During training only, a reward measures how much the agent's self-written world knowledge improves later task success. The trained agent gains 20 percent on WebVoyager and WebWalker tests, and a compact 14-billion-parameter model beats an unassisted Gemini-2.5-Flash.
arxiv-2604-18231: Abdollahi and seven colleagues present AgenTEE, a system for running language-model agents privately on edge devices. Cloud hosting leaks latency and privacy, yet edge devices face software attacks and hostile owners. AgenTEE isolates the runtime, inference engine, and third-party apps in separately attested confidential virtual machines. Built on Arm's Confidential Compute Architecture, it keeps proprietary prompts and weights safe at near-native speed.
arxiv-2604-18331: Du, Grannen, Song, and Sadigh test whether a robot quadruped can work as an enjoyable running trainer. The SNOOPIE pacerbot runs interval sessions tuned to each runner's ability, competing against a wearable trainer in user experiments. Runners stuck to pace schedules about 61 percent better with the robot and held steadier speeds. Participants also strongly preferred the robot on ease of use, enjoyability, and helpfulness, suggesting physical presence adds real value to exercise coaching.
arxiv-2604-18631: Sole tests old metronome marks for Beethoven's five piano-cello sonatas against over one hundred recordings from 1930 to 2012. Czerny's and Moscheles's marks fall short of the whole set, with gaps of 15 to 39 percent. Kolisch's 1943 marks track recorded practice far more closely than either rival set. Allegro speeds stay steady across eight decades, since slow, middle, and fast habits live side by side, with the middle one on top. From the set's most common speeds, he offers new marks as ranges mirroring expert practice, not single fixed values.
arxiv-2604-18731: Bhagwat and three colleagues use SPICE simulations to test how bursty versus smooth stellar feedback shapes early galaxies, traced by the bright carbon-II line. All models tie carbon-II luminosity tightly to star formation rate, but bursty feedback gives lower luminosity at a fixed rate and larger scatter. Emission extends well beyond ultraviolet light, and fast outflows add little to it, so carbon-II kinematics can misread gas speeds. Gas kinematics still separates the models, with smooth feedback settling disks earlier and yielding higher disk fractions.
arxiv-2604-18831: Wu and three colleagues study whether indoor lidar semantic segmentation can be learned by distillation from a visual foundation model. Acquiring ground truth for lidar is costly, yet visual foundation models segment image frames well. The team couples lidar scans with a processed camera image to train a lidar model by 2D to 3D distillation. Evaluated on indoor SLAM data sets with pseudo labels, the distilled model reaches 56 percent mean IoU. Against real labels it reaches about 36 percent, showing cross modal distillation works without manual annotations.
arxiv-2604-19331: Cunningham, Greene, Cross, and Rago build a formal test for judging whether summaries of parliament debates carry their arguments in full. Debate volume and complexity strain outside audiences, and auto scores match human checks for truth poorly. Their approach, driven by computational argumentation, grounds argument structures in the contested proposals under debate. The test aims to make large-scale debate summary checks possible rather than merely fluent.
arxiv-2604-19431: Buda, Primiero, Ceragioli, and Antonelli introduce CTLF, a branching-time logic for reasoning about bias in generative AI output series. Generative AI amplifies biases in training data, yet inference-time fixes stay mostly empirical and lack formal guarantees. In CTLF, each world stands for a possible output at a given step. Modal operators check whether the output series respects an intended distribution over a protected attribute. The logic predicts the odds of staying within bounds as new outputs arrive, and counts how many outputs must be removed to restore fairness.
arxiv-2604-19631: Wang and colleagues propose MoSA, a motion-guided semantic alignment method for dynamic scene graph generation. Such work models objects and their dynamic interactions in video at a high level. Current methods struggle with fine-grained relationship modeling and tail links. MoSA encodes object-pair motion attributes like distance, velocity, persistence, and directional consistency, then fuses them with spatial features to yield motion-aware representations.
arxiv-2604-19831: Fazlollahi proposes an extension of general relativity based on the van der Waals equation of state, bringing non-ideal thermodynamic effects into gravity. Under Jacobson's thermodynamic reading of gravity, where field rules arise from the Clausius relation, the approach yields modified field rules with a varying effective coupling. That coupling evolves with the traits of the underlying system. It has major consequences in high-energy regimes, including a natural way to avoid the initial singularity of standard Big Bang cosmology.
arxiv-2604-19931: Singh and four colleagues compared three ways to teach data science students to write hints for faulty code. Students wrote hints alone, with AI help on demand, or with AI help held back until after a first draft. In a trial with 97 graduate students, the held-back design gave the best hints and helped students catch errors they would otherwise miss. Students prized the task for debugging practice and for learning to judge AI output with care.
arxiv-2604-20131: Subbiah and five colleagues study positionality and bias in LLM digests of life stories, asking how machine interpretation shapes study conclusions. Deductive coding can be checked against human labels, but abstractive thematic analysis resists such direct judgment. Their summary pipeline surfaces perspective-taking biases an LLM may employ, showing both race and gender bias with potential representational harm. The authors urge future LLM-interpretation studies to include a positionality portrait of the study's stance.
arxiv-2604-20531: Yeginbergen, Oronoz, and Agerri test multilingual medical question answering across high-resource languages, English, Spanish, French, and Italian, and low-resource Basque and Kazakh. They compare three evidence types: curated medical repositories, web-retrieved content, and explanations from a language model internal knowledge. Larger models lead in English at baseline, and English web-retrieved evidence helps high-resource languages most. For low-resource languages, combining English and target-language retrieval matches high-resource accuracy, showing that the best evidence strategy depends on language resources and model scale.
arxiv-2604-20631: Bianchi, Jacquier, and Sfragara work on the Ising model over a two-community stochastic block model, where spins split into two groups. They characterize the diagram and show that the model undergoes a uniqueness transition of the Gibbs measure. In the supercritical regime, the magnetization vector law converges to a mixture of Dirac measures. If alpha-n is much greater than 1/n, it sits on two points; if at most about 1/n, on four. In uniqueness, they analyze magnetization fluctuations in the subcritical regime and prove a quenched CLT.
arxiv-2604-20731: Vilkha, Służalec, Łoś, and Paszyński present a solver for CO2 sequestration. The solver uses IGA-ADS for the saturation field update explicitly, and CRVPINN for the pressure field. The study simulates the behavior of CO2 in porous structures, excluding chemical reactions, with the model based on Darcy's Law. CRVPINN is pretrained on the pressure configuration, and each time step update requires only 100 iterations of the Adam method. Compared with an IGA-ADS plus MUMPS baseline, the hybrid solver is over 3 times faster on a node.
arxiv-2604-20831: Chau, Zhao, Laflorencie, and Meng study the ground-state phase diagram of a spin-1 Heisenberg chain with staggered long-range interactions. They use a quantum Monte Carlo approach based on the split-spin representation. They resolve the continuous quantum phase transition between the gapped Haldane phase at large alpha and a gapless Neel phase at small alpha, where the continuous SU(2) symmetry is broken. From finite-size scaling and crossing point analyses, they determine the critical point at alpha_c equals 2.49 and extract critical exponents.
arxiv-2604-21131: Ari Azarafrooz exposes a blind spot in AI-agent safety: guardrails judge each message alone, so an attack split across dozens of sessions slips past every detector. His CSTM-Bench supplies 26 executable attack taxonomies with matched benign confounders across two 54-scenario splits. Both a session-bound judge and a full-log correlator lose about half their attack recall on the harder split, while a bounded-memory reader keeping the 50 highest-signal fragments survives both.
arxiv-2604-21431: James Hipperson, Jonathan Hargreaves, and Trevor Cox build JAX-BEM, a boundary element solver with gradient tracking that brings machine-learning-style automatic differentiation to acoustic shape tuning. Old-style tuning struggles with many goals and parameters, but JAX-style systems track gradients through fast linear algebra. Their solver matches existing BEM codes' error on a benchmark and enables gradient-based geometry tuning. Though shown acoustically, the concept extends readily to electromagnetic waves.
arxiv-2604-21731: Chai uses enhanced Langlands data to sort out irreducible representations of twisted p-adic general linear groups in unramified principal series. The paper defines standard ones and proves the twisted Kazhdan-Lusztig conjecture for counts in the Grothendieck group. It mainly follows Lusztig's connected-case work using graded Hecke algebra. The resulting parametrisation matches the Whittaker-normalized one. The work gives a complete list for this family of groups. That list helps researchers work with these groups in practice.
arxiv-2604-21831: Kawałek and Krzaczkowski build a single algebraic frame for circuit complexity beyond the Boolean domain. Old results focus on Boolean circuits, partly because computers are built that way. Richer circuit landscapes over larger domains get lost in that focus. Building on Barrington's branching programs and nonuniform deterministic automata, and on Idziak's wider version, they sort out which languages circuits over simple algebras recognise, and over algebras from congruence modular varieties.
arxiv-2604-21931: Wu and eight colleagues treat time as a learnable visual concept in videos. They learn, self-supervised, to spot speed changes and gauge playback speed. Those models then assemble the biggest slow-motion video collection yet from noisy in-the-wild sources. Slow-motion footage from high-speed cameras holds richer temporal detail than standard video. Using this data, they build models for temporal control, including generation conditioned on speed and super-resolution over time for blurry low-FPS videos.
arxiv-2604-22131: Benhaida, Drissi, and Saidi place the Haldane model on the dice lattice, changing next-nearest-neighbour flow and breaking inversion and time-reversal symmetries. They find point-charge particle symmetries at π/6 and 5π/6 and derive analytic quasi-energy forms. Gap closure at these points drives a topological transition, confirmed by Berry curvature and magnetic moment. Chern numbers for the valence, flat, and conduction bands shift with flux ties: equal fluxes give (2, -2, 0) then (0, 2, -2), while differing fluxes give (-1, -1) and (1, 1). Hall conductivity shows a quantized plateau of 2σ₀, a tilted plateau sliding from 1.50σ₀ to about 1σ₀.
arxiv-2604-22231: Mandal and Chaudhuri extend Jurin's law to fluids that make their own internal stress. The classic law gives how high liquid climbs in a narrow tube. Their theory adds an active stress term at the liquid surface. A new height formula then follows from activity strength and alignment at the meniscus. Depending on those factors, activity can raise, lower or fully suppress the climb.
arxiv-2604-22631: Herron and three colleagues typify two kinds of phoneme error in speech recognition systems. Modern speech recognition systems work better for certain speaker groups than others. One barrier to fairer systems is understanding errors, particularly embedding differences between high- and low-performance groups. The framework distinguishes random error, high phoneme variance, from systematic error, embedding bias. Training phoneme probes only on a single disadvantaged group sometimes improves performance for that group, evidence of group-level bias in phoneme embeddings. Speakers and groups with higher phoneme variance match lower-performance groups.
arxiv-2604-22931: Noonan and twelve colleagues report JWST observations of main-belt comet 457P/Lemmon-PANSTARRS, active in 2020 and again in 2024. Earlier JWST results on two outer comets supported water reservoirs as drivers, but 457P orbits closer in, within the 5:2 resonance with Jupiter. Despite dust activity in ground and JWST images, the team finds no water, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, or methanol within tight limits. They suggest 457P is more depleted than its companions; wider surveys will tell whether it is an edge case or a distinct subclass.
arxiv-2604-23331: Wu and Beerel propose Branch Landing, a forward-edge control-flow integrity framework for RISC-V that replaces checks with Bloom filter queries. Two ISA extensions carry a source Section Identifier through a register and validate it at landings with latency independent of source count. Granularity spans type-based to CFG-derived policies. On 81 BEEBS benchmarks, overhead stays under half a percent and code growth near half a percent. The CFG-derived policy cuts equivalence class size by 32.5 percent against the type-based policy, with no failures.
arxiv-2604-23431: Scholl and colleagues reconstruct in-plane magnetization patterns in thin magnetic films from scanning NV magnetometry, a technique that maps stray fields above the sample. Because many magnetization patterns could produce the same field, they guide a simple autoencoder with spatial masks that narrow the search, needing no pretrained data. Aligning those masks well sharpens the result markedly, and tests on patterned Permalloy structures back the approach.
arxiv-2604-23531: Katanyukul simplifies Eigenmarking, a quantum search refinement that keeps answer states in the minority so Grover amplification can work, and flags the no-answer case with complementary states. Earlier schemes needed either two extra qubits or a hard multi-qubit controlled rotation, but his version needs only one extra qubit and a standard two-qubit controlled rotation. Two-qubit simulations show it beats both earlier marking schemes on both reported measures.
arxiv-2604-23631: Pizzuti and colleagues test chameleon gravity, a modified-gravity family with screening, using joint lensing and kinematic mass profiles of nine massive galaxy clusters. With cuspy mass profiles the combined constraints match general relativity and rule out large parts of the theory's parameter space. A cored profile instead hints at a mild departure, but the tension eases once dynamically disturbed clusters are excluded.
arxiv-2604-24131: Luo and five colleagues spot encryption loops in binary-only ransomware by checking the avalanche effect itself. Earlier work only checked a ripple effect, a necessary but insufficient sign, which attackers can fake. Their record-and-replay method tolerates sloppy input and output identification and resists evasion, backed by Shapiro-Wilk normality guarantees. Tests show no missed cases and 1.1 percent false alarms, and the tool analyzes every sample drawn from ten representative ransomware families.
arxiv-2604-24231: Filiot, Joseph, Pérez, and Sunny give the first complexity theory for Hanoi Omega-Automata, the standard omega-regular automata format for synthesis tools. Its succinct symbolic form, with Boolean transition guards and transition-based coloring, makes problems harder. Non-emptiness is NP-complete under standard conditions, with hardness from the Boolean guards. Language inclusion is PSPACE-complete mostly but EXPSPACE-complete for Emerson-Lei acceptance. The authors formalize Hanoi Omega-Games, with bounds from Pi-2-completeness to PSPACE-completeness, and extend techniques to symbolic games over decidable theories.
arxiv-2604-24531: The CMS team searches for Higgs bosons produced together with two vector bosons through vector boson scattering. The data come from proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. Events were chosen with two forward jets, a large jet from a boosted Higgs decay to bottom quarks, and up to two charged leptons. The team excludes a range of values for the coupling modifier linking two vector bosons to two Higgs bosons, giving a new probe of that interaction.
arxiv-2604-24631: Zhang, Zhang, Ren and Yang apply a model-independent method for measuring the Weyl potential, which describes how gravity bends light, to KiDS-1000 lensing plus BOSS and 2dFLenS galaxy clustering. Fitting late-time observables in two redshift bins, they find one galaxy sample sits below the general-relativity prediction while the other matches it. A mild lensing-is-low hint appears, yet gravity tests overall show no significant preference for modified gravity.
arxiv-2604-25031: Amrollahi, Lopez and Barrett propose roundtrip checks for faithful formalization. Their approach formalizes a claim, translates it back, re-formalizes, and uses a tool to check match. Disagreement triggers stage diagnosis pinpointing the error step, with scoped repair attempting correction. They evaluate on the Texas Transportation Code and the Texas Parks and Wildlife Code, with two models and three baselines. Diagnosis-guided repair proves most effective, tied to diagnosis reliability. Under full repair, rules failing the equivalence check show up to 2.5 times more inference drift than rules passing it.
arxiv-2604-25231: Iyengar and six colleagues introduce DRAGON, a benchmark for evidence-grounded visual reasoning over diagrams. Diagram question answering needs models to interpret charts and maps, yet correct answers do not guarantee grounding. Given a diagram, a question and the answer, a model must predict bounding boxes for the elements justifying the answer. The data set holds 11,664 instances from six diagram data sets, with human-verified evidence annotations. Even Claude Opus 4.6 reaches a Grounding IoU of only 23.8 percent on AI2D, so faithful grounding remains an open challenge.
arxiv-2604-25631: Nair and Ferrie build fast, cheap, good classical tensor-train surrogates for fully trained quantum machine learning models in local patches of input space. Repeated circuit runs during inference bottleneck quantum machine learning, and the frame answers with Taylor polynomial approximation in tensor-train form. The Taylor-TT build certifies that the hypothesis class holds a good approximation. Three error sources stay controllable on their own: Taylor truncation, tensor-train approximation, and sampling error. Parameter counts scale with data dimension, separating representation complexity from feature-induced constants.
arxiv-2604-25931: Lathkar identifies anchored confabulation in large language models. One verified middle fact in a multi-step chain raises the confident-wrong-answer rate before full evidence removes it. A partial anchor pushes the model toward confident completion of remaining steps. The author formalizes the effect as Parametric Hallucination Confidence. Six lines of evidence support it, including causal injection and capability scaling tests. An anchoring threshold law predicts amplification by hop depth. For retrieval routing, a learned router closes about 81 percent of the oracle gap.
arxiv-2604-26631: Hinlopen and seven colleagues demonstrate a programmable superconducting diode built from the nematic superconductor FeSe. Ordinary diodes of this kind fix their one-way behavior in sample shape or crystal structure, making them static circuit parts.
